title: Linkability of sensor data to user
description: Wearable device links multiple data points (GPS, heart rate, timestamps) to uniquely identify the user, enabling tracking across contexts.
assumptions: Device processes and correlates telemetry data internally.

title: Inference of sensitive health conditions
description: Device infers private health information (e.g., stress levels, medical conditions) from continuous sensor telemetry.
assumptions: Telemetry data contains patterns correlatable to health states.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure in transit
description: Sensor telemetry intercepted during transmission between user and device (e.g., via insecure wireless protocols).
assumptions: Data transmitted over potentially unencrypted channels.

title: Data integrity violation in transit
description: Sensor data altered during transmission (e.g., GPS spoofing, heart rate manipulation).
assumptions: Transmission lacks integrity checks or encryption.

title: User unaware of data collection scope
description: User may not fully understand the extent or purpose of continuous sensor data collection.
assumptions: Privacy notices are unclear or overlooked during device setup.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Wearable device transmits raw GPS traces and device IDs beyond what is necessary for the companion app's functionality, violating data minimality.
assumptions: Device sends full sensor batches without aggregation or anonymization.

title: Identifiability via Data in Transit
description: Unencrypted transmission of GPS traces and device IDs allows interception and linkage to a specific user.
assumptions: Data flow lacks encryption or secure transport mechanisms.

title: Linkability Across Sessions
description: Device ID and timestamps enable correlation of multiple exercise sessions to a single user across time.
assumptions: Device ID is persistent and not anonymized per session.

title: Non-Compliance with Legal Requirements
description: Companion app processes GPS data without explicit user consent or fails to adhere to data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR).
assumptions: App lacks transparent consent mechanisms for sensitive data processing.

title: Health data aggregation creates detailed user profiles
description: The companion app aggregates multiple manual entries of calorie intake, meals, and weight over time, creating comprehensive health profiles that reveal sensitive patterns about the user's lifestyle, eating habits, and physical condition.
assumptions: App stores and processes historical health data entries

title: Health data could identify the user
description: Weight entries, meal patterns, and calorie tracking data could potentially be used to identify the user, especially when combined with other data sources or through pattern analysis.
assumptions: Health data contains identifying characteristics or can be linked to other identifiers

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: The companion app could disclose the user's health data (calorie intake, meals, weight) to third parties without explicit consent, such as advertisers, data brokers, or other services.
assumptions: App has data sharing capabilities with external parties

title: User unaware of data usage implications
description: The user may not be fully aware of how their manually entered health data will be used, stored, or shared by the companion app beyond the immediate logging function.
assumptions: User consent process may not fully explain data usage

title: User cannot intervene in data processing
description: Once health data is submitted to the companion app, the user may have limited ability to control how it is processed, analyzed, or shared with other systems.
assumptions: App processes data automatically after submission

title: Explicit Data Disclosure
description: Location History Store collects and stores GPS traces with timestamps, potentially exceeding data minimization principles if continuous tracking is not strictly necessary for app functionality.
assumptions: Assumes location data collection is not fully justified by app purpose

title: User Identifiability
description: Stored GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked to specific users, enabling identification and profiling.
assumptions: Assumes location data is stored with user identifiers or can be correlated with other user data

title: User Unawareness
description: Users may not be adequately informed about continuous location tracking and storage practices, limiting informed consent.
assumptions: Assumes app lacks clear privacy notices or granular consent mechanisms

title: Regulatory Non-compliance
description: Location data collection may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) if purpose limitation, consent, or data minimization requirements are not met.
assumptions: Assumes app operates in jurisdiction with strict data protection laws

title: Data Linkability
description: GPS traces in transit could be intercepted and correlated with other data sources to infer user behavior or identity.
assumptions: Assumes data flow lacks encryption or secure transmission protocols

title: Health data linkability across sessions
description: The Health Analytics Service can link calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions to create comprehensive health profiles, potentially enabling identification of individuals through behavioral patterns even if individual records are anonymized.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to historical session data and can correlate patterns

title: Individual identification from health patterns
description: Health condition analysis using calorie, weight, and exercise data could identify specific individuals through unique health patterns, especially when combined with other data sources or demographic information.
assumptions: Health patterns are sufficiently unique to enable identification

title: Implicit data disclosure to third parties
description: The Health Analytics Service may share derived health insights or raw health data with third parties (e.g., insurance companies, researchers, advertisers) beyond the original purpose of health-condition analysis, violating data minimality principles.
assumptions: Analytics service has capability to share data externally

title: User unawareness of cross-session health analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across multiple sessions for health-condition analysis, or may not understand the scope and implications of this processing.
assumptions: User consent and notification mechanisms are inadequate

title: Health data processing non-compliance
description: The Health Analytics Service's processing of sensitive health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) may not comply with applicable regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection laws.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements apply to this health data processing

title: Location history disclosed to analytics service
description: The Location History Store shares personal location data with the Health Analytics Service. This represents a data disclosure across system boundaries. Under the minimality principle, this disclosure should only occur if strictly necessary for the analytics purpose.
assumptions: Location history contains personal data that could identify individuals through movement patterns

title: Individuals identifiable through movement pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service derives daily routines and movement patterns from location history. These patterns can be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources or temporal analysis.
assumptions: Movement patterns are sufficiently unique to identify individuals

title: Location data linkable with other health data
description: The analytics service may link location history with other health-related data, creating comprehensive profiles that reveal sensitive information about individuals' health conditions, behaviors, and routines.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to or can correlate with other personal data

title: Users unaware of location pattern analysis
description: Individuals may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed to derive movement patterns and daily routines. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent about how their data is being processed.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly explain pattern analysis purposes

title: Potential GDPR purpose limitation violation
description: Analyzing location history for movement patterns may exceed the original purpose for which location data was collected. This could violate purpose limitation principles under GDPR and similar privacy regulations.
assumptions: Location data was originally collected for different purposes than pattern analysis
uncertainty_note: Depends on original consent scope and data collection purpose

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management in data flow
description: The data flow DF8 may lack adequate security controls (e.g., encryption, access controls) for transmitting sensitive health analytics, leading to non-compliance with regulations like GDPR or HIPAA.
assumptions: Assumes regulatory requirements mandate secure transmission of health-related data.

title: Profiling a group of individuals via analytics data
description: Health analytics insights (e.g., trend flags, risk indicators) sent by P3 could enable the app (P2) to infer group-level characteristics from individual data, linking the user to broader populations.
assumptions: Assumes analytics data includes patterns that can be aggregated to profile groups.

title: Unauthorized viewing of sensitive health indicators
description: The app dashboard displays sensitive health risk indicators (eating disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user. If the user's device screen is visible to others (e.g., in public spaces, shared environments), this could lead to unauthorized disclosure of highly sensitive health information to third parties who observe the display.
assumptions: User may use the app in environments where others can see their screen; no additional access controls on the dashboard view

title: Interception of health data in transit
description: Health risk indicators and trend data transmitted from the app to the user's device could be intercepted during transmission if not properly encrypted, exposing sensitive medical information to network attackers.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over network connections that may not be fully secured

title: Inference of sensitive health conditions from displayed data
description: The app infers and displays eating disorder or diabetes risk signals based on user data. These inferences themselves constitute sensitive health information that could reveal conditions the user may not have explicitly disclosed or may not be aware of, creating privacy risks through data deduction.
assumptions: Inference algorithms process user data to generate health risk indicators; these inferences are displayed without user consent for the specific inference

title: User unawareness of data processing implications
description: Users may not fully understand how their health data is being processed to generate the risk indicators displayed, or what the implications are of receiving these inferences. This lack of awareness could prevent informed consent and appropriate privacy decisions.
assumptions: Dashboard may not provide clear explanations of how risk indicators are derived or what data sources are used

title: Non-compliance with health data protection regulations
description: Displaying inferred health conditions (eating disorder or diabetes risk) may violate healthcare privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR special category data requirements) if proper consent, security measures, and data minimization are not implemented. This creates legal and organizational risk.
assumptions: Health risk indicators constitute protected health information or special category data under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details

title: Unnecessary data sharing to third-party cloud provider
description: Full health and location dataset is shared with external cloud provider, potentially exceeding minimality principle.

title: Re-identification risk from health data
description: Health data may allow re-identification of individuals if not properly anonymized.
uncertainty_note: Assumption based on typical third-party risks; specific anonymization controls unknown.

title: Linkability of location data
description: Location data could be linked with other datasets to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Assumption based on typical third-party risks; specific data linkage controls unknown.

title: Unauthorized data access at cloud provider
description: Cloud provider may have insufficient security controls, leading to data disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Assumption based on typical third-party risks; specific security measures unknown.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Cloud provider may not comply with applicable privacy laws (e.g., GDPR).
uncertainty_note: Assumption based on typical third-party risks; specific compliance status unknown.
